title: Poland unveils significant new home storage subsidy - Energy Storage
content: Poland’s Ministry of Climate and Environment has announced a $257.9 million (PLN 1 billion) subsidy scheme for home battery and heat storage, aimed at increasing self-consumption from residential solar and other renewable energy installations. The program is open to individuals with grid-connected home solar or other small renewable electricity systems. It will subsidize batteries with at least 10 kWh of capacity and heat storage tanks holding at least 100 liters. Batteries must provide at least 2 kWh of storage per kWp of the accompanying solar installation. The scheme will cover the costs of purchasing and installing home storage systems. Battery grants will cover up to 30% of eligible costs, capped at approximately $206 (PLN 800) per kWh. Prosumers in the net-billing system can receive up to approximately $4,126 (PLN 16,000), while those in the net-metering system can receive up to approximately $2,063 (PLN 8,000). Applicants can receive up to 30% of eligible costs for EU-manufactured heat storage systems, capped at approximately $258 (PLN 1,000). An additional bonus of up to approximately $516 (PLN 2,000) is available for an EU-manufactured battery or a necessary replacement EU-manufactured hybrid inverter. Total support is capped at approximately $4,900 (PLN 19,000) per electricity supply point. The scheme is financed through the Modernization Fund. Applications will open on October 20 and close on October 1, 2027, or when funds are exhausted. Poland’s Minister of Climate and Environment, Paulina Hennig-Kloska, said equipping residential solar installations with energy storage is a ministerial priority. “The program has two main goals: increasing the efficiency of renewable energy use and strengthening energy security,” she added. According to the ministry, the number of home energy storage systems in Poland rose from more than 10,000 in the first quarter of 2024 to around 150,000 in June 2026, supported by subsidies and market growth. The ministry is targeting more than 200,000 home storage systems by the end of 2027. Sławomir Ćwik, deputy minister of climate and environment, said eligible battery installations must include an energy management system and backup power capability. “This allows households to maintain power even during grid outages,” Ćwik said. An initial phase of support financed through Poland’s National Recovery Plan allocated approximately $28.9 million (PLN 112 million) to support the installation of more than 5,000 home battery systems, according to the ministry. Poland’s Agency for Restructuring and Modernization of Agriculture recently announced a renewable energy subsidy scheme aimed at farmers. It opened for applications on October 5. Following Australia In Australia, the Federal government similarly offered a 30% subsidy on home installations of residential batteries , without a monetary or kWh cap, or need for existing solar installation, though some restrictions were added to cap the total installation sizing. The scheme has been budgeted to approximately AU$7.2 billion (US$4.68 billion or PLN 18.15 billion), and has seen more than 500,000 households add storage, or some 13 to 14 GWh of behind-the-meter storage capacity. title: Aula Energy plans 1.8 GWh BESS for 330 MW of solar in Australia - Energy Storage
content: Aula Energy, the renewables dedicated offshoot of finance giant Macquarie Asset Management, has unveiled plans to build a AUD 350 million ($242 million) battery energy storage system (BESS) at the site of the 330 MW Wellington North Solar Farm in New South Wales, Australia. The proposal is for a 365 MW BESS with five hours of storage capacity that Aula Energy said will enable excess power generated during peak production periods to be stored and dispatched when required, improving the overall efficiency of the PV plant while helping to strengthen grid reliability. “The proposed modification will support the optimisation of the solar farm and network electricity generation,” the company said, adding that “battery storage is an essential part of Australia’s renewable energy transition. Combining battery storage with solar farms helps overcome the intermittent nature of renewable energy by storing excess power when production is high and releasing it during peak demand. This ensures a steady supply of power at all times.” The Wellington North Solar Farm, located about 7 km northeast of Wellington within the Central West Orana Renewable Energy Zone of New South Wales, has been fully operational since mid-2024, generating about 778,654 MWh of renewable electricity per year. It is located alongside the 174 MW Wellington Solar Farm that commenced operations in late 2020. Both the Wellington North and Wellington solar farms are owned and operated by Aula following an acquisition earlier this year. Aula Energy said the proposed BESS would be located within previously cleared land used for a laydown for the construction of the Wellington North Solar Farm. The system would include approximately 288 battery containers, 96 storage inverters, 96 transformers, 96 power conversion systems, and a new 33 / 330 kV substation. The battery would make use of the existing 8.3 km 330 kV high voltage transmission line that connects the solar farm to the Wellington substation. “By building on established infrastructure, the project is designed to strengthen the energy system while making better use of existing infrastructure,” Aula Energy said. The Australian-headquartered renewable energy business is targeting financial close in early 2027, subject to regulatory and commercial considerations. Aula’s proposed battery is part of a growing move in the Australian utility-scale energy market with the standalone solar farm no longer the default project structure. The Australian Energy Market Operator’s (AEMO)  Connections Scorecard for the June quarter shows batteries are the dominant technology in the 75 GW development pipeline, representing 53% of capacity, while hybrid solar-plus-battery projects account for 18% of total capacity. At the same time, the developers behind 2.4 GW of solar projects commenced or completed processes to add a BESS, reflecting the industry’s growing interest in combining renewable generation with flexible storage. title: EDP targets 350 MW of BESS in Sicily - Energy Storage
content: EDP said it has an 800 MW pipeline of renewable energy projects in Sicily, with battery energy storage systems (BESS) accounting for the largest share at about 350 MW, followed by solar with 250 MW and wind with 200 MW. The group told pv magazine Italia that it has already invested about €220 million ($246.6 million) in the island and built 152 MW of renewable energy capacity. EDP said its utility-scale solar projects currently operating in Sicily total 71 MW, representing a combined investment of €65 million. A further €15 million in capital expenditure is allocated to projects currently under development in the region. The development status of the pipeline varies. EDP said several projects have reached relatively advanced stages after completing key permitting and development steps, while others remain in the early stages. Overall, EDP expects to progressively develop the pipeline over the next three to five years, depending on market mechanisms, permitting processes, grid connection availability and market conditions. The company expects to invest between €250 million and €400 million during this period, continuing to focus on a balanced portfolio of solar, onshore wind and energy storage. EDP said energy storage is taking on an increasingly important role in its development strategy for Sicily. title: BW ESS, Danske Commodities sign 10-year optimization agreement on 857 MWh Berkswell BESS - Energy Storage
content: BW ESS has signed a 10-year revenue-floor and optimization agreement with Denmark’s Danske Commodities for its 200 MW / 857 MWh Berkswell battery energy storage project in the UK. The agreement covers the entire asset, which entered construction in September and is expected to become operational in the fourth quarter of 2027. Located near Solihull in the Midlands, Berkswell is co-owned with AIP Management and is expected to use Sungrow’s PowerTitan 3 technology. The deal follows a similar agreement with BW ESS and EDF in April , covering the 350 MW / 1,243 MWh first phase of BW ESS’s Hams Hall project. BW ESS has now secured 10-year revenue floors for two of its larger UK batteries, both designed for several hours of discharge. Neither announcement disclosed the floor level or how revenues above it would be shared, or detailed the deeper extent of the agreement. “This agreement with Danske Commodities provides a strong commercial foundation for Berkswell and helps unlock the long-term value of this strategically important energy storage project,” said Kilian Leykam, chief commercial officer of BW ESS. “With construction under way, we are another step closer to bringing the project online and delivering critical flexibility to the UK grid.” “We are proud to have been selected by BW ESS to optimize Berkswell,” said Jakob Sørensen, CEO of Danske Commodities. “Drawing on more than 15 years of experience in British power markets, we will use our trading expertise to maximize the value of the asset while providing the flexibility needed to integrate intermittent renewable generation. The UK is a core market for us, and Berkswell is an important addition to our growing portfolio of flexible assets.” The post BW ESS, Danske Commodities sign 10-year optimization agreement on 857 MWh Berkswell BESS appeared first on Energy Storage .

title: Origin plans 4.9 GWh battery expansion in Australia - Energy Storage
content: Australia’s biggest energy retailer is seeking federal environmental approval to build an eight-hour battery energy storage system (BESS) that will add 500 MW of capacity to the battery precinct being built next to the Eraring power station on the New South Wales (NSW) Central Coast. Origin is seeking approval under the federal Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation (EPBC) Act for the Eraring BESS North project that proposes the construction of a battery with a discharge capacity of 500 MW and an accessible energy storage capacity of about 4,942 MWh. In its EPBC referral, Origin says the project responds to “structural shifts in the National Electricity Market (NEM) as the electricity sector transitions from coal-fired generation toward variable renewable energy, supported by dispatchable firming capacity such as electricity storage.” “The development of large-scale BESS projects is critical to the ongoing transition to renewable energy,” Origin said. “The NSW Electricity Infrastructure Roadmap targets at least 12 GW of renewable generation and 2 GW of long-duration storage by 2030, while the Australian Energy Market Operator’s 2024 Integrated System Plan forecasts that the NEM must triple grid-scale variable renewable energy by 2030, creating a firming gap that this project will help address.” The Sydney-headquartered utility said the Eraring BESS North would operate in conjunction with the existing Eraring BESS precinct that is being built in stages. The 460 MW / 1,770 MWh first phase of the Eraring BESS was connected to the National Electricity Market (NEM) at the start of 2026 and construction is continuing on the 240 MW / 1, 390 MWh second stage that is due to come online early in 2027. While the public numbers don’t add up, Origin said in its scoping report that once complete, the Eraring BESS will comprise an energy storage capacity of approximately 3,658 MWh. Together, the existing and proposed BESS facilities would provide a combined maximum registered active power capacity of about 1,200 MW and a combined accessible energy storage capacity of approximately 8,600 MWh. “This dispatchable capability decouples the project’s output from weather-dependent generation profiles, allowing it to serve periods of high demand independent of wind and solar conditions, particularly during evening peak hours,” Origin said. Construction of the Eraring BESS North project is planned to be launched in 2028, with commercial operations scheduled for early-to-mid 2031. Origin said the Eraring North BESS will contribute to its commitments to achieve net zero by 2050 and support its shift away from coal . The 2.88 GW Eraring power station, the nation’s largest coal-fired generator, is scheduled to close in April 2029. title: Mixed self-assembled monolayer enables 18.88% efficiency in 5.2 cm² inverted perovskite solar cell - pv magazine Global
content:
Researchers at the
Indian Institute of Technology Bombay
have fabricated a large-area inverted perovskite solar cell based on a mixed self-assembled monolayer (SAM) that improves perovskite film quality, enhances charge transport, reduces interfacial recombination losses, and increases device efficiency and stability.
SAMs have emerged as key components in high-efficiency perovskite solar cells, particularly in inverted architectures, where they serve as ultrathin hole-selective contacts that improve charge extraction and reduce interfacial recombination losses. Previous research has shown that SAMs can also
enhance device stability and mechanical reliability
, while optimizing energy-level alignment between the perovskite absorber and the underlying electrode. More recently, scientists have developed
co-assembled SAM strategies
to improve surface coverage, suppress defects, and promote better perovskite crystallization. Further advances in
SAM molecular engineering
have enabled efficiencies approaching 27%, highlighting their potential for developing efficient, stable, and scalable perovskite solar cells.
“We have developed a mixed-carbazole-based SAM strategy for wide-bandgap perovskite solar cells, targeting both surface wettability and suppression of non-radiative recombination at the buried interface. By combining different carbazole-based SAMs, we were able to tune the interfacial properties and promote improved perovskite film formation for the scalabilty of device,” corresponding author Dinesh Kabra told
pv magazine
. “The impact of the mixed-SAM interface on perovskite film formation and charge-carrier recombination was systematically investigated using morphological and optical characterization.”
The scientists explained that scaling perovskite solar cells from laboratory-scale devices of around 0.1 cm² to larger areas remains a major challenge, particularly for inverted (p-i-n) architectures with wide-bandgap (WBG) absorbers. Although significant efficiency improvements have been achieved in small-area devices, increasing their size typically results in substantial performance losses.
With this in mind, they developed a mixed SAM combining [4-(3,6-dimethyl-9H-carbazol-9-yl)butyl]phosphonic acid (Me-4PACz) and [4-(7H-dibenzo[c,g]carbazol-7-yl)butyl]phosphonic acid (4PADCB). While Me-4PACz provides favorable energy-level alignment, low interfacial defect density, and efficient hole extraction, 4PADCB improves wettability and promotes more uniform perovskite crystallization and larger grain formation.
The team built the solar cell with a glass and indium tin oxide (ITO) substrate, a hole transport layer (HTL) based on the mixed SAM, a perovskite absorber, an aluminum oxide (AlOx) interlayer, a fullerene (C60) electron transport layer, a tin oxide (SnOx) buffer layer, and a silver (Ag) metal contact.
The researchers said the mixed-SAM approach combines the favorable electrical properties of Me-4PACz with the improved film-forming characteristics of 4PADCB, resulting in better device performance and uniformity.
In cells with an active area of 1.2 cm², the mixed-SAM configuration achieved a power conversion efficiency of 20.30% and a fill factor of 81.23%, compared with efficiencies of 18.17% and 19.30% for devices using Me-4PACz and 4PADCB alone, respectively. Surface and morphological analyses revealed improved wettability, more compact perovskite films, larger columnar grains, and fewer interfacial defects. Photoluminescence mapping and conductive atomic force microscopy also indicated more homogeneous optoelectronic properties and improved local charge transport.
When the active area was increased to 5.2 cm², the mixed-SAM cell achieved a maximum efficiency of 18.88%, compared with 17.20% and 17.96% for devices based on Me-4PACz and 4PADCB alone, respectively. The larger mixed-SAM cells also maintained an average efficiency of 17.81%, compared with 18.96% for their smaller counterparts, with limited device-to-device variation.
Further analysis showed that the efficiency losses associated with scaling were mainly attributable to increased series resistance at other interfaces and in the transparent conductive oxide electrode, rather than changes in intrinsic recombination characteristics.
Under damp-heat testing at 85 C and 65% relative humidity, the cells took more than 680 hours to fall to 75% of their initial efficiency. According to the researchers, the results demonstrate that mixed-SAM interface engineering can improve efficiency, stability, and reproducibility while limiting performance losses in large-area inverted perovskite solar cells.
“Importantly, the present study isolates interface- and area-dependent losses using a consistent spin-coating process; the solution-processable nature of the mixed-SAM strategy provides potential compatibility with scalable deposition techniques, such as blade coating, slot-die coating, and spray coating, which represent important pathways toward further scale-up and module-level fabrication,” the academics concluded.
The device was described in “
Mixed Carbazole Self-Assembled Monolayers Enable Scalable Large-Area (>5 cm2) Efficient Wide Bandgap Perovskite Solar Cells
,” published in
ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces

title: Albania’s next solar auction to include storage - pv magazine Global
content:
Albania is planning to run a new solar auction, with battery storage included for the first time.
The country’s Minister for Infrastructure and Energy, Enea Karakaçi, confirmed the government is preparing another auction to take place before the end of this year, or in early 2027.
Karakaçi added the auction will be developed in cooperation with the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development.

. The following two were both won by French developer Voltalia, covering a
140 MW project
100 MW project
respectively.

. A total nine bids
were shortlisted
, with eight securing contracts covering 283.9 MW of the procured capacity.
The addition of storage into the next solar auction follows changes to the country’s electricity law, which now facilitates the inclusion of battery energy storage systems into renewable energy projects.

title: Utility solar generation reaches record highs in Australia - pv magazine Global
content:
The latest data from global energy consultancy Rystad Energy shows that Australia’s fleet of large-scale solar and wind assets generated 5.44 TWh of clean energy last month, an increase on the 4.99 TWh generated in
and up 7% from the 5.1 TWh recorded in September 2025.
Rystad senior analyst David Dixon said Victoria was the biggest contributor to the monthly total with the state’s utility-scale solar assets generating a record 276 GWh of clean energy while its wind assets produced 1,250 GWh – a total of 1,526 GWh.
Dixon said utility PV generation also reached record highs in New South Wales (NSW) and Queensland, totalling 841 GWh and 645 GWh respectively.
Curtailment of solar dropped year-on-year with 22% of available generation in the National Electricity Market (NEM) curtailed last month, compared to 26% in September 2025.
Acen Australia’s 400 MW Stubbo Solar Farm, in central west NSW, was ranked Australia’s top-performing PV facility for the month with an average AC capacity factor (AC CF) of 35%.
The 162 MW Columboola Solar Farm, owned by South Korea’s Hana Financial Investment, and the 204 MW Edenvale Solar Park, co-owned by Japanese companies Eneos and Sojitz, also notched 35% AC CF.
The performance of the Stubbo Solar Farm, which commenced full commercial operations in late 2025, coincided with the recent arrival of a mob of 250 sheep at the site as part of Acen’s
shared land use approach
that supports grazing, land management, and bushfire preparedness alongside renewable energy generation.
“Agriculture and renewable energy don’t need to compete for land,” the developer said. “At Stubbo Solar, we’re proud to demonstrate how farming and clean energy generation can work hand in hand, supporting local agricultural practices while delivering renewable energy into Australia’s electricity network.”
Acen said the integration of sheep grazing helps keep the land productive while providing practical benefits for site management.
“It’s a simple but effective example of how renewable energy projects can continue to support agricultural activity and create shared value for regional communities,” the company said.
While solar generation continued to reach record high, wind generation in September 2026 was flat or down relative to the same time last year in all states except Queensland.
Wind generation for September 2026 was down about 86 GWh compared to September 2025 while about 13% of available generation in the NEM was curtailed.
The top-performing wind assets for the month were the Flat Rocks facility in Western Australia with a 55% CF, followed by the Cattle Hill and Graville Harbor wind farms in Tasmania, with 49% and 48% CF respectively.

title: Forecasting domestic U.S. module production to the end of 2027 - pv magazine Global
content:
Following an incredible two days at
Solar Manufacturing USA 2026
in Austin, Texas on 22-23 September, all the intel gathered regarding the U.S.-specific production and capex plans of more than 60 manufacturers has now been digested and analysed.
Overlapping with the official release of the new Solar Manufacturing USA Quarterly report, during this week, one aspect of the report’s key findings will be presented and discussed every day on
pv magazine
Kicking off this special Austin-debrief series of articles, Part 1 looks at domestic U.S. production volumes to the end of 2027.
Forecasting production bottom-up is the bedrock of market research
The Austin event was pivotal on many fronts, with the 400+ attendees likely each having a unique subset of reasons why the event was needed and how it could help shape what comes next with domestic U.S. solar manufacturing.
One of my hopes is that the event could put an end to the past few years of U.S. solar market observers adding up announced capacity numbers or placing pins in maps every time someone is cited with an aspirational factory investment desire.
Adding announced capacities in the solar industry is naïve, unhelpful and misleading. Ditto, collating random investment figures only detracts from the real picture.
The Solar Manufacturing USA Quarterly report tracks and forecasts (to the end of 2030) the domestic solar manufacturing capex and production volumes for 40-plus companies (and set to grow in 2027), making up more than 99% of value-chain production to the end of 2027 at least.
Production and capex at the company level is split into specific manufacturing sites, expansion phases, technology, effective ramped capacity, capacity conversion rates (aka utilization), production outputs – all at the quarterly level. Capex is further segmented into contributions each quarter at the site/expansion level across buildings/infrastructure, production equipment and upgrades/maintenance contributions.
Forecasting production bottom-up is the bedrock of market research
Forecasting module production to the end of 2030 at the company level is one of the most important outputs from the new report. More than simply the total production volumes by quarter, and year, one can then look company-by-company and estimate the total volumes available for new third-party module procurement in the 4-year window 2027-2030.
U.S. module buyers are less interested in total volumes; rather, which companies will have module availability for projects in this period.
Each manufacturing company has its own set of criteria here. First Solar, for example, has the longest pipeline of committed domestic output. Others, such as Illuminate and Canadian Solar, have in-house commitments to downstream project activities. Then we have companies that are focusing more on rooftop or small commercial shipments only and by default are not in the running for 100-500 MW project business.
Finally, many of the companies are new to the manufacturing space – some even being altogether new companies with no track-record of commercial operations.
Therefore, it is truly a mixed bag of module availability if you are looking for secure supply of high-volume domestic-produced modules in, for example, the 2028-2030 period. Having knowledge at the company level outweighs the overall market metrics for production, far less the meaningless capacity-counting analyses that have plagued the U.S. sector since the IRA was introduced at the end of 2022.
Forecasting module production volumes over the next 12-18 months also has its own set of challenges, except for a few exceptions that are running factories today with strong backlog commitments.
Imported cell volumes, at least according to the monthly United States International Trade Commission (UTITC) numbers, are looking decidedly on the low side of recent, as per the HTC codes accumulated. This may get corrected over time. Therefore, the overall 2026 volumes – leading up to December in particular – are still to be known, even if stockpiling becomes an issue and can be proven at the company/importer level.
Good luck to those tasked with this challenge. Even if 232 had not come into force during 2026, there was inevitably going to be a significant second-half import uptick considering the new ramped capacity being rolled out across a wide range of existing and new market entrants. Each now must prove their cell import uptick (relative to historic volumes) is a consequence of having more effective module capacity, or being a new entrant altogether, and not simply to stockpile cells ahead of the MIP coming into effect. Goodness knows how much time and effort is going to be spent on this side issue in the first few months of 2027.
One of my takes from Austin last week was the business-as-usual approach from many c-Si module producers for 2027 – namely to keep buying cells from overseas, albeit at 20-something cents and hopefully sell modules at 40-something levels. And try make the books work as best as possible.
What choice do these companies have? New cell factories take 12-24 months to come online in the United States, and even if a suitable location/shell-building can be found, upfront costs ahead of production are not small change.
Tomorrow’s Austin-debrief article will show the new analysis for cell production to the end of 2027. Suffice to say now that 2027 – the first year post-232 – could easily end up being a record year for c-Si solar cell imports. What does that say about U.S. trade policy in helping domestic manufacturing, some five years on from the Inflation Reduction Act being introduced?
Let’s leave for now with the module production forecast for 2027. The headline numbers may be record-module production metrics, but the reality is still a fragmented landscape desperately trying to release capital into new factories and have some form of certainty that profitability and long-term growth can be provided.
I have shown the forecast in module production to Q4 2027, back to Q1 2025, in the figure below. The upside reflects a production-led scenario, assuming sufficient cell volumes are indeed imported during 2027. Conversely, the downside forecast would kick in if the market is constrained either from project offtake volumes being lower than production targets or from a push-back on buying cells under MIP conditions.

title: Real-world testing via the AMMONEX pilot, laboratory R&D to overcome engineering and process challenges in ammonia cracking
content:
Real-world testing via the AMMONEX pilot, laboratory R&D to overcome engineering and process challenges in ammonia cracking
In our latest episode of Project Features, we focused on ammonia cracking: both how engineering & process challenges are being worked through to enable deployment at industrial scale, and how these and other lessons are being applied to pilot projects like Duiker’s under-construction AMMONEX pilot at the Port of Rotterdam. Jebin James (Development Lead, Duiker Clean Technologies), Mathias Galetz (Director, DECHEMA-Forschungsinstitut), and Hilbert Keestra (Postdoctoral Researcher, University of Twente) were joined in conversation by AEA Technology Manager Kevin Rouwenhorst. The recording is available on our website, and you can also download the speaker slides here.
Duiker’s AMMONEX Pilot
Duiker Clean Technologies is a market leader in combustion process solutions for sulphur recovery, and is now licensing ammonia cracking technology and supplying proprietary equipment for ammonia cracking plants. Duiker’s Low-NOX ammonia combustion system (Stoichiometric Controlled Oxidation or SCO) has been used in refineries since 2009 to convert ammonia-containing offgases, using staged combustion with dynamic air control to minimise NOX emissions. The same combustion technology is integrated into Duiker’s ammonia cracker, which consists of three main steps: the proven SCO technology, a heat integrated ammonia cracking reactor operating at mild temperatures and with a Nickel-based catalyst, and a gas separation unit.
Duiker’s ammonia cracking technology is a simple and compact design with a focus on high energy efficiency and a high single pass ammonia yield, while producing hydrogen at elevated pressure. Ammonia can be used as fuel in the SCO unit, resulting in no CO2 emissions. Steam is not required as an input and will not be produced as a co-product.
Temperature is one of the determining factors in the design of ammonia cracking technologies, as a high temperature results in a higher single pass ammonia conversion, but a lower temperature minimizes nitriding risks, creating a trade-off. Duiker utilizes a Nickel-based catalyst rather than a Ruthenium-based catalyst, because (1) Ruthenium-based catalysts typically require low pressure operation for optimal performance, and (2) Ruthenium has limited availability and is expensive (at around $62,000 per kilogram currently). However, Nickel-based catalysts operate at higher temperatures (typically 650-800 °C), which can require more expensive materials for the reactor tubes and other equipment. Ruthenium-based catalysts typically operate within a lower and narrower temperature range (400-525°C). The ability of a reactor design to accommodate different catalyst operating temperatures is therefore an important consideration in view of future catalyst developments.
Duiker Clean Technologies will operate an industrial-scale pilot plant for its ammonia cracking technology in the Netherlands. The Netherlands Enterprise Agency (RVO) is supporting the project under the DEI+ scheme, with co-financing from the EU via the Just Transition Fund (JTF). Construction is underway, and Duiker expects to proceed with testing in 2027. In 2026, Duiker Clean Technologies chose the Port of Rotterdam as the location for the installation of the AMMONEX ammonia cracking pilot plant. A core part of the pilot plant is to verify the performance of ammonia cracking catalysts and materials of construction, both of which are crucial for long-term industrial-scale deployment of a commercial plant.
For the AMMONEX ammonia cracking pilot, Duiker has assessed 17 catalyst suppliers, with 5 shortlisted based on their techno-commercial performance. Further bench-scale testing was performed in partnership with catalyst vendors, with up to 2 wt.% water added to the ammonia feedstock, and thermal cycling experiments were performed. For reference, commercial grade anhydrous ammonia contains 0.2-0.5 wt.% water to prevent stress corrosion cracking. The intrinsic kinetics were measured under industrially relevant conditions for ammonia cracking, e.g. at elevated pressures and with water content in the ammonia feedstock. A reactor model was built on this basis. The AMMONEX pilot will validate the catalyst performance, verify activation and passivation procedures at industrially relevant scale, and will allow for feedback to vendors for further catalyst improvement.
The AMMONEX pilot will also allow for real-world testing of the various materials used in construction: a total of 14 candidate materials and coatings cover the full length of the reactor to test their long-term performance (plus the 4 candidate materials and coatings selected for the superheater). These materials and coatings need to be stable long-term upon various start-up and shutdown cycles.
Engineering & process challenges being addressed by R&D
Nitriding
The high-temperature and pressurized conditions for ammonia cracking indicate that selecting the right material or coating for the reactor tubes is key to maximize material lifetime. Ammonia production typically occurs at temperatures below 550°C, meaning stainless steels like 316L are suitable. However, higher temperature conditions for ammonia cracking means a different material is required.
During cracking, various phenomena may occur, namely nitrogen embrittlement (nitriding), hydrogen embrittlement, and corrosion in the presence of moisture (H2O). Among these phenomena, nitriding during cracking is the most important. Nitriding occurs when ammonia reacts on the reactor tube surface, releasing hydrogen as a gas (H2) but with nitrogen (N) penetrating into the metal instead of forming nitrogen as a gas (N2).
Above 550°C, Iron-rich alloys become highly susceptible to nitriding. Historically, high Nickel-alloys have been used for the reactors of ammonia crackers in the heavy water industry. The most commonly used alloy, Inconel 625, contains at least 58 wt.% Nickel, around 20-23 wt.% Chromium, plus other components. The protective, Chromium-rich initial oxide layer cannot sustain and delays nitriding during an incubation time before nitriding will occur. This nitriding behaviour is initially very fast, but progresses via a parabolic curve over time, as diffusion-limited thickening of the nitriding layer slows penetration into the material. Upon significant penetration in the material, the mechanical integrity of the tubes can be compromised.
The DECHEMA-Forschungsinstitut in Germany has performed numerous tests with metallic alloys over the past years, using a laboratory set up with alumina crucibles. Generally, high Nickel-alloys have the lowest nitriding susceptibility. Tests at 600°C, 700°C, and 800°C indicate varying temperature effects. What makes it complex is the interplay of the activity of the different species on the surface, thermal cracking in the gas, as well as higher nitrogen diffusion rates into the material at higher temperatures. A higher operating pressure also changes the nitridation rates.
For example, at 800°C, the nitriding behavior of all materials was less than at 700°C, which can be explained by the increased thermal decomposition of ammonia, resulting in less nitrogen availability on the material surface in the form of nitrogen molecules. Gaseous nitrogen (N2) does not exhibit significant nitriding behaviour at these conditions, and the ammonia-hydrogen ratio decreases, which makes nitriding less favourable. This effect also indicates that nitriding is less prevalent toward the end of an ammonia cracking reactor (assuming the same temperature), because of the higher catalytic conversion of ammonia to hydrogen and nitrogen under these conditions.
Ammonia cracking kinetics
Commercial ammonia cracking catalysts include Iron-based catalysts, Iron-Cobalt alloy-based catalysts, Nickel-based catalysts, and Ruthenium-based catalysts. Ammonia crackers at heavy water production facilities (operating at pressures up to 150 bar) typically use Iron-Cobalt alloy-based catalysts. Significant focus for newbuild ammonia crackers using commercial grade ammonia is on Nickel-based catalysts and Ruthenium-based catalysts.
The choice of catalyst will determine the performance of the ammonia cracking reactor. Relevant aspects include its stability, and its activity under the relevant temperatures, pressures, and water contents.
Most research focuses on individual datasets, with a single catalyst, and usually with measurements at atmospheric pressure, and without water.
Researchers from the group Catalytic Processes & Materials at the University of Twente in the Netherlands have developed “unified” kinetic models for Nickel-based catalysts and Ruthenium-based catalysts, based on 20 datasets for Nickel-based catalysts, and 14 datasets for Ruthenium-based catalysts (985 experimental data points at pressures in the range 1-99 bar). Additionally, datasets for Nickel-based catalysts with up to 80 wt.% water were used to determine the effect of water on the catalytic activity. Using this approach, robust kinetic models can be derived that are less dependent on the data quality of a single dataset.
The research found that nitrogen recombination on the catalyst is the slowest reaction step for most Nickel-based catalysts, while NH dehydrogenation was found to be the slowest reaction step for most Ruthenium-based catalysts. Trends versus pressure indicate that especially the Ruthenium-based catalysts significantly decrease in activity at high pressures, primarily due to hydrogen inhibition on the catalyst surface.
The water content in commercial grade anhydrous ammonia negatively impacts the catalyst performance of commercial ammonia cracking catalysts. The model for Nickel-based catalysts indicates that a variation in water content in the commercial grade anhydrous ammonia (range 0.2-0.5 wt.%) may lead to changes in ammonia cracking performance. Lower temperatures also result in more water inhibition of the catalyst.

title: AM Green secures renewable ammonia offtake for 10 years
content:
AM Green secures renewable ammonia offtake for 10 years
H2Global auctioned renewable ammonia supply to reach Germany from 2029
India-based renewable ammonia producer AM Green Ammonia has successfully won a bid to supply the Asia lot of renewable ammonia in H2Global’s latest auction round. The cost of this long-term purchase agreement is a minimum €585 million over 10 years. The subsidies will be managed by HINT.CO (Hintco) (via public funding from the German Government), who will recoup the cost by re-sale of the Renewable Fuels of Non-Biological Origin (RFNBO) to offtakers in German and European markets from 2029.
The renewable ammonia production is planned to occur at AM Green’s Kakinada project (specifically Phase 2, Phase 1 offtake is split between Uniper and Yara) in Andhra Pradesh. The fossil fuel-based ammonia plant is being refitted with alkaline electrolysis technology, powered by a renewable energy network that is backed up by pumped-hydro supply. The produced renewable ammonia will be exported from neighbouring Kakinada Seaports.
This result shows a market gaining rapid momentum. Strong bids from serious developers have demonstrated the growing maturity of renewable ammonia projects since the pilot tender. A long-term contract gives producers like AM Green the certainty to invest and secures reliable supply for European buyers. We thank every bidder and hope to see them in future rounds.
Timo Bollerhey, CEO of Hintco and Co-Founder of H2Global, in AM Green’s official press release, 30 Sep 2026
Repeated disruptions to fossil fuel supply chains have been felt worldwide. Renewable ammonia carries clean power across oceans to industries that cannot be fully electrified, with little or no carbon emissions. H2Global is bringing together governments and industry to build resilient global supply chains for clean energy and commodities.
Markus Exenberger, Executive Director of the H2Global Foundation and Co-Founder of H2Global, in AM Green’s official press release, 30 Sep 2026
We are immensely proud that AM Green has been selected as the winner of the H2Global Asian lot. This landmark achievement consolidates AM Green’s position as the supplier of choice for renewable ammonia to Germany and wider Europe, and demonstrates that optimally priced green molecules can be delivered from India at an industrial scale. Winning through a binding competitive process is a strong validation of the readiness of our platform. From Kakinada, we will deliver renewable ammonia to European and Asian customers, turning ambitious decarbonisation targets into real industrial emissions reductions. This is an important milestone for AM Green, and only the beginning of the role we intend to play in building a global market for renewable molecules.
Mahesh Kolli, Group President and Joint Managing Director of AM Green, in his organisation’s official press release, 30 Sep 2026
There are three other H2Global tenders still to be awarded in this round, segmented into regional lots as follows: Africa, South America & Oceania with €484 million available for each.
You can learn more about how H2Global sees its role in developing early renewable fuel markets and industry tipping points observed during the adoption of previously new technologies that are commonplace today.
In the H2Global auction process, Hintco runs a competitive process where renewable ammonia producers bid to secure long-term purchase agreements for renewable ammonia. The committed funds de-risk early-moving projects by supporting Financial Investment Decision (FID) or other project milestones. Similarly, an auction is run for the selling of the renewable ammonia purchased, where offtakers commit to buying the renewable ammonia for a price the market deems competitive. The difference in supply and demand cost is paid by public money accumulated by Hintco to achieve a double-action auction mechanism such that reliable commitment to both demand and supply for renewable ammonia initiates industry growth.

title: Next-generation, high-efficiency electrolyser attracting global interest
content:
Next-generation, high-efficiency electrolyser attracting global interest
Hysata announces engineering agreements, government grants, first customers and commercial demonstrations
InterContinental and Hysata engineering agreement formalised
After 4 years of unofficial collaboration, Australia-based Hysata and Singapore-based InterContinental Energy have officially entered an engineering agreement to explore the potential for integration of Hysata’s electrolyser technology into giga-scale hydrogen projects. .
InterContinental is a global renewable fuels developer, known for its patented, modular P2(H2)Node™ hydrogen production system architecture. InterContinental is also targeting installation of this production system at giga-scale on land that experiences premium solar and wind exposure and locating electrolyser and ammonia production facilities in the near vicinity to minimise transmission costs and losses. Hysata brings its capillary fed electrolyser technology, operating at 95% efficiency or needing 41.5kWh of electricity to produce 1kg of hydrogen. Hysata reports that this is a 20% improvement compared with any commercially available electrolyser on the market, translating to approximately 120,000 more tons of renewable ammonia (or US$100 million at current price) per 1GW of renewable electricity capacity utilised. The electrolyser design has been influenced by InterContinental’s findings as the P2(H2)Node™ developed.
As reported, the first phase of the official agreement is that Hysata will deliver performance data for the P2(H2)Node™ as a Digital Twin Optimisation Network. This will provide data for optimisation of location choice, node configurations and components and project output based on the renewable energy available. The digital twin data improves design certainty, therefore minimising capital and operating costs by up to 20% which combines to increase confidence for investors and interested parties.
Hysata’s differentiated technology offers the step change electrolysers need to drive down the cost of green hydrogen. High system efficiency dramatically reduces the amount of power a project consumes, which cuts both capex and the levelised cost of hydrogen. These are big projects, and we’re excited to be involved.
Paul Barrett, CEO of Hysata, quoted in Fuel Cell Works, 24 Sep 2026
Standardisation is how green fuels reach giga-scale. This collaboration enables us to model and optimise Hysata’s ultra-high-efficiency electrolyser technology within the P2(H2)Node™ framework, giving developers greater cost and performance certainty for large-scale projects.
Alex Tancock, CEO of InterContinental, quoted in Fuel Cell Works, 24 Sep 2026
Hysata commissions manufacturing capacity in Australia, announces government funding
Last month, Hysata launched HysataFab, a manufacturing platform for the production of its next-generation electrolysers, located at its 8,500m2 Port Kembla headquarters near Wollongong, Australia. HysataFab consists of three production lines for electrodes, membrane, cell and stack. The electrode production line was also commissioned on the same day. HysataFab uses real-time monitoring, robotics and inline testing with AI to increase electrode manufacturing efficiency by up to 15%. Once the platform is fully operational the predicted electrolyser manufacturing rate is 200MW per year which is scalable with increasing demand owing to the modular nature of the design.
At the same launch, the Australian Renewable Energy Agency (ARENA) announced a AU$49 million grant towards the establishment of Hysata’s electrolyser manufacturing capability. This was awarded under the Government’s Future Made in Australia Innovation Fund.
This project is a major jobs and economic opportunity for the Illawarra and helps ensure Australia makes more of the clean-energy technology the world needs. Hysata’s electrolyser can help reduce the cost of hydrogen production and decarbonise energy-intensive sectors like steel, fertiliser and heavy transport. Making electrolysers here in Australia is a huge opportunity to strengthen our manufacturing capability, back local innovation, create skilled jobs and seize a bigger share of the global clean-energy technology market.
Chris Bowen, Minister for Climate Change and Energy of the Australian Government in Hysata’s press release, 23 Sep 2026
First commercial order
Three months ago, Hysata received the first commercial order for its next-generation, high efficiency electrolysers from an undisclosed customer. This moved the five year old company’s proven technology into the category of commercial product. The order will be manufactured at the Port Kembla plant on the new production line.
Commercial demonstration agreement with Saudi Arabia’s ACWA Power
And since early 2025, Hysata has been working with Saudi Arabia-based ACWA Power to deploy a commercial-scale demonstration of its next-generation electrolysis technology in Saudi Arabia.
ACWA Power capital projects include the 2.2GW, 600 tons of hydrogen per day NEOM green hydrogen project in Saudi Arabia, scheduled to be operational in 2026. Such expertise and offtake potential will fast track the development of Hysata’s electrolysers.
Our agreement with Hysata marks the beginning of a mutually beneficial and strategically important partnership. Combining ACWA Power’s extensive experience in developing and operating large-scale energy projects with Hysata’s cutting-edge electrolyser technology, creates a powerful synergy to drive significant progress in the green hydrogen sector. This partnership will be instrumental in achieving our shared long-term vision of a sustainable and decarbonised energy future, contributing to both economic diversification and environmental stewardship in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and globally. It solidifies our commitment to the ambitious goals outlined in Saudi Vision 2030 and strengthens our position as a leader in the global energy transition.
Marco Arcelli, CEO of ACWA Power in Hysata’s press release, 10 Feb 2025

title: BasiGo and its fleet of electric buses
content:
10 Climate Tech Companies to Watch 2026
See the full list
BasiGo aims to replace the tens of thousands of diesel-powered buses on sub-Saharan African roads with electric ones that generate far fewer emissions. The company’s pay-as-you-drive business model has helped make EVs more attainable and is changing the way public transport operates.
In a bid to contain the covid-19 pandemic in 2020, the Kenyan government temporarily suspended public transportation. The suspension lasted only three days, yet the change in air quality was dramatic. The air was so clear that Mt. Kenya—Africa’s second-highest peak—was visible in Nairobi, roughly 175 kilometers away. Some could even spot Mt. Kilimanjaro, the continent’s highest mountain, even farther in the distance.
This reprieve from smog sparked the idea for BasiGo’s electric bus business. The company’s founders glimpsed what could happen to the air if diesel buses and trucks were cleaned up. Since then, they’ve built a fleet of more than 100 electric buses to lease to customers who are operating them in Kenya and Rwanda. These buses have ferried 15 million passengers since BasiGo’s founding.
The company doesn’t manufacture its own buses—the vehicles come from China and are assembled in Kenya. BasiGo’s innovation lies in offering a full range of services that make its electric buses more competitive with internal combustion engine (ICE) buses, says Jit Bhattacharya, co-founder and CEO. Instead of simply selling its buses to operators, as other bus companies do, BasiGo leases them out, offers maintenance services and insurance, and provides a charging network for its customers. Those customers are primarily individual operators or bus cooperatives, of which there are more than 300 in Kenya.
Key indicators
Industry:
Electric vehicles
Founded:
Headquarters:
Nairobi, Kenya
Notable fact:
BasiGo is the first authorized service provider in sub-Saharan Africa for CATL, the world’s largest EV battery company. Its own buses use CATL batteries and BasiGo’s employees are trained to repair the batteries on other vehicles.
Potential for impact
The initial price of electric buses is very high compared to combustion-engine models. Electric vehicle expenses are lower over the long term, though, because of the savings from fuel. BasiGo’s model aims to remove the barrier of high up-front cost for private bus operators in Africa looking to add an electric bus to their fleet.
Under this approach, the operator pays a small deposit, which Bhattacharya says is 40% less than the down payment they would make on a diesel bus. The operator then pays a daily pay-as-you-drive lease fee. Bhattacharya estimates the operator earns a 5–10 times higher return on investment over the life of a BasiGo bus compared to a diesel bus.
When it comes to emissions, Bhattacharya and his team calculate that replacing one diesel bus with an electric one in Kenya results in 50 tons of avoided carbon dioxide emissions every year. With about 20,000 buses currently operating in Nairobi alone, transportation emissions could be dramatically reduced if every bus was electric.
Since its buses run on domestically generated renewable energy (90% of Kenya’s energy mix is renewable), operating them will keep more money in the local economy compared with fuel, which has to be imported. And switching to EVs also has potential health benefits, such as a decrease in childhood asthma cases, due to less particulate matter in the atmosphere.
BasiGo buys many of the parts for its buses from Chinese firms including King Long and BYD. But the buses have to be locally assembled in Kenya. So the company must spend a lot of time and resources training personnel to build, repair, and maintain the buses in every location in which it operates—which could be a challenge for any future expansion.
The company also faces high up-front costs for infrastructure upgrades required to support new high-power loads such as EV chargers. And Bhattacharya says securing land for charging depots is “expensive and complicated” since charging requires land located directly on bus routes and next to power lines.
Next steps
At the moment, more than 150 BasiGo buses are on the road, and the company has a reservation list of 1,200 customers who wish to lease vehicles as more become available.
Having already expanded from commuter buses to providing inter-city coach services, BasiGo is now targeting the next big polluters on the roads: trucks. The company has not yet announced any details about its plans, but says to stay tuned.

title: Moment Energy and its shipping containers packed with old EV batteries
content:
Moment Energy and its shipping containers packed with old EV batteries
The startup is betting that repurposing—rather than recycling—used EV batteries will help buoy much-needed US supply.
Demand for energy storage is surging, with capacity expected to grow eightfold in the next decade. To meet that demand, Moment Energy wants to shortcut a supply chain that now flows largely through China, by domestically repurposing EV batteries into new grid-connected storage systems.
Moment Energy’s four founders met while studying mechatronics engineering in college and worked together on a team that built and raced electric cars. After graduating, they scattered to companies including Tesla and Apple, but aimed to someday work together again.
Then, after two tornadoes tore through parts of Ottawa in 2018, taking hospitals and cell towers offline—and putting the now-CEO through his first full-scale power outage—the foursome sensed an opportunity. The team began disassembling Nissan Leaf batteries in a garage in British Columbia and repackaging them to deliver backup systems to homes and businesses. The battery business was growing quickly: in 2019, just as Moment Energy launched, battery storage capacity was expected to balloon 40 times by 2040.
Today, their vision looks prescient. Disasters including hurricanes and wildfires continue to spur blackouts, and booming data center demand has expanded the market for energy storage even further. Moment now works with tech companies looking for ways to manage their power supply as well as customers preparing for potential outages.
Ongoing trade battles between the US and China have been a shot in the arm for the company. Nearly all battery manufacturing is rooted in China and batteries imported to the United States face steep tariffs (though the future of some of those duties remains uncertain). Meanwhile, Moment will soon be able to categorize its repurposed batteries as domestic products in both Canada and the US, where it’s building its next plant. The company also claims to be the only “second life” battery company to receive important certifications from independent safety evaluator UL, which financiers and insurers use to evaluate whether a battery system is a secure investment.
Key indicators
- Industry: Battery repurposing
- Founded: 2019
- Headquarters: Vancouver, Canada
- Notable fact: The company’s bylaws contain a promise that it will never send a battery to a landfill.
Potential for impact
Last year, the world deployed 1.2 terawatt-hours of electric vehicle battery capacity, according to the International Energy Agency. And while EVs account for the great majority of battery use worldwide, battery storage is now the fastest-growing power technology.
Producing all of those batteries, though, is resource-intensive: The minerals must be mined and processed, manufactured into a final product, and then shipped (often from China) to ports around the world. What’s more—when an EV reaches the end of its useful life, as much as 80% of the car’s battery capacity remains.
Recycling is an expensive process, and the great majority of battery recycling capacity is in China. So battery materials from North America must be shipped back across the ocean to be stripped of useful minerals and metals. (Though the Trump administration in August said it would ban this practice, in a bid to stem the stream of critical materials headed for recycling in China.)
Repurposing can bridge initial use and recycling. After Moment receives a used battery pack, the company screens each cell for health and safety, plugging metrics into proprietary AI models that quantify its remaining life, and recycles any cells that are not up to snuff. The rest are linked together and repackaged in 20- or 40-foot-long steel containers. Moment’s systems are designed to extend a battery’s useful life for another 10–30 years. Global warming potential, resource use, and impacts to human health are all reduced when repurposing a battery before recycling it, according to a 2023 analysis.
More than one million EV batteries worldwide could reach the end of their lives by 2030. Moment says that its model could reroute more than two gigawatt-hours of batteries from landfills or recycling facilities every year.
Today, Moment represents a tiny slice of the overall energy-storage market. The company has deployed 11 systems since its founding, initially for off-grid homes and more recently for grid-connected hospitals, airports, and other commercial and industrial facilities that need additional power supply or want to avoid costly system upgrades for new power sinks like EV chargers.
How significantly the company can scale will depend, in large part, on the stream of EV batteries it can obtain and how quickly it can test and repackage them. Today, the company sources used batteries from around 20 car companies, including Nissan and Mercedes-Benz.
Moment must also compete against cheap, new batteries flowing in from China. The company says its systems now cost under $90 per kilowatt-hour. Average costs for energy-storage batteries reached $70 per kilowatt-hour in early 2026. Even when accounting for tariffs and shipping costs, some new batteries may still undercut repurposed models.
Next steps
In June, the company cut the ribbon on its Megafactory 1 in Vancouver. Slated to repurpose one gigawatt-hour of battery capacity per year by 2030, it is the world’s largest facility for repurposing EV batteries. It took just six weeks to bring the facility online.
Using funds from the US Department of Energy and part of the $100 million the company has raised thus far from investors including Amazon and Liberty Mutual, Moment is now finishing an even bigger facility in Texas. Even together, though, the two hubs will be able to process only a fraction of the batteries retiring from North American roads. To realize its full climate potential, the startup will need to sustain its early momentum and scale up dramatically.

甲骨文(Oracle)拟采购Point Beach核电站电力，为威斯康星AI数据中心供电
2026年10月5日，美国科技巨头甲骨文公司(Oracle)宣布，计划从威斯康星州(Wisconsin)的波因特比奇核电站(Point Beach Nuclear Power Station)采购125兆瓦至250兆瓦电力，为波特华盛顿(Port Washington)的大型人工智能与云计算数据中心园区供电。该采购协议仍需威斯康星州公共服务委员会(Public Service Commission of Wisconsin)批准。
据了解，甲骨文将获得该双机组核电站总输出约10%至20%的电力。甲骨文表示，这一承诺将帮助客户免受核电站成本上升影响，减轻家庭电费压力，并维持威斯康星电网可靠供电，预计可为客户节省约3亿美元;波特华盛顿数据中心的成本将由甲骨文全额承担。
波因特比奇核电站拥有两台591兆瓦西屋电气(Westinghouse)压水堆(Pressurised Water Reactor, PWR)机组，Point Beach-1于1970年12月投入商业运行，Point Beach-2于1972年10月投运，位于密歇根湖(Lake Michigan)畔的Two Rivers，是威斯康星州唯一核电容量，满足该州约15%电力需求。2025年，美国核管会(Nuclear Regulatory Commission, NRC)将Point Beach-1运行许可延长至2050年10月，Point Beach-2延长至2053年3月，使电站寿命达到80年。
该电站原由We Energies拥有，2007年出售给独立能源基础设施巨头新纪元能源(NextEra Energy)，但We Energies继续购买其大部分电力。当前购电协议2033年到期，We Energies近期签署协议，将继续购买该电站约86%电力，为期20年。甲骨文云基础设施(Oracle Cloud Infrastructure)执行副总裁马赫什·蒂亚加拉詹(Mahesh Thiagarajan)表示，“甲骨文正在作出承诺，将直接惠及超过100万威斯康星公用事业客户。通过吸收约3亿美元上升的能源成本，我们帮助保护威斯康星电力用户，同时支持该州依赖的可靠、无碳电力。”
据悉，若获得批准，该协议将成为科技公司直接锁定现有核电容量、为AI数据中心供电的又一案例，有助于缓解威斯康星电网压力并稳定电价。

谷歌拟与星座能源达成超10亿美元购电长协：锁定现役核电基荷以支撑AI算力扩张
近日，谷歌母公司Alphabet正深入推进与美国最大的商业核反应堆运营商星座能源公司(Constellation Energy Corp.)的商务洽谈，双方即将正式敲定一份多年期核电采购协议(Power Purchase Agreement, PPA)。该交易总金额预计至少达到10亿美元，若磋商进展顺利，最快有望于本周内正式对外发布。
当前，人工智能技术的迭代演进引发了全球算力集群与超大规模数据中心用电需求的爆发式攀升。由于新建大型商业核电站涉及极为漫长的许可证审批与工程建造周期，科技巨头普遍将目光聚焦于具备24小时不间断基荷供电能力的现役核能资产，通过注资机组扩容、增购基荷配额等形式锁定稳定且无碳的电力资源。
针对正在推进的磋商细节，谷歌与星座能源双方在周一均未予以公开置评。目前，该协议所涉及的具体承购电量规模、挂钩机组的技术参数以及对应的核电站地理选址等关键商业条款仍处于保密阶段，尚未对外披露。
此前，星座能源已于9月30日同亚马逊(Amazon)达成了为期20年的长期供电合作。根据该项协议，星座能源将对其位于马里兰州的卡尔弗特克利夫斯核电站(Calvert Cliffs Nuclear Power Plant)投资实施190兆瓦(Megawatt, MW)的功率提升工程(Power Uprate)，并向亚马逊定向交付包含扩增容量在内的690兆瓦核电基荷，反映出科技资本全面重塑核电资产商业模型的新趋势。

美国与韩国航运巨头联手探索核动力汽车运输船项目
2026年10月6日，韩国现代格罗维斯(Hyundai Glovis)与美国利宝环球物流(Liberty Global Logistics)签署谅解备忘录(MOU)，宣布将共同开发核动力纯汽车专运船(Pure Car and Truck Carrier, PCTC)，以推动跨太平洋等韩美核心贸易航线上新能源动力船舶的创新应用。
据报道，本次合作由现代格罗维斯高管金泰宇(Taewoo Kim)与利宝环球物流总裁大卫·米内蒂(David Minetti)共同推进并签署协议。双方计划借助先进的海洋核能技术，探索在韩美贸易航线上建立核能运输枢纽与高效低碳的汽车物流供应链。
据了解，纯汽车专运船作为全球远洋汽车运输的核心船型，面临着日益严格的国际海事组织(IMO)碳减排与脱碳监管压力。核动力系统具备零排放、续航里程长以及无需频繁加注燃料等显著优势，被视为远洋大型商船实现深度脱碳的重要前沿技术路径。
据悉，美韩两国此前已在陆基大型反应堆及模块化核能领域达成了多项战略合作，此次双方将核能应用延伸至民用海事航线，标志着美韩在海洋核动力(Marine Nuclear Power)商业化应用与绿色航运物流领域的合作迈出了实质性的一步。

芬兰赫尔辛基推进城市核能供热项目 拟建欧洲首座市中心供暖小堆
2026年10月6日，芬兰首都赫尔辛基(Helsinki)正推进利用核能为城市区域供热(District Heating)。能源公司海伦(Helen)正在评估建设供热能力达400至500兆瓦的小型模块化反应堆(Small Modular Reactor, SMR)，候选地点包括萨尔米萨里(Salmisaari)、沃萨里(Vuosaari)以及东松德姆(Östersundom)的诺尔贝里特(Norrberget)。
据报道，赫尔辛基计划在2040年前彻底结束基于化石燃料燃烧的能源生产，核能供热由此成为其区域供热系统实现深度脱碳的关键选项之一。芬兰核能初创企业稳定能源(Steady Energy)已在萨尔米萨里一座废弃燃煤电厂的汽轮机大厅内建造LDR-50供热反应堆原型机，并于2026年2月完成了首罐混凝土浇筑。该原型机设计热功率为50兆瓦，不配备汽轮机与发电机组，而是将核裂变产生的热量通过换热器直接注入城市供热管网。目前正在测试的原型机暂未装载核燃料(Nuclear Fuel)，而是采用电加热元件模拟热源，以全面验证全尺寸下的冷却与被动安全功能。
据了解，LDR-50反应堆运行温度约150摄氏度，显著低于用于发电的常规反应堆，系统设计与建造更为简化，未来的商业化装置拟采取地下埋设方式。欧洲投资银行(European Investment Bank, EIB)已于2026年9月承诺向稳定能源提供高达4000万欧元的融资支持，用于技术研发、测试及许可证申请，这也是该行首次直接资助SMR技术。稳定能源计划在2030年代实现首批商业化装置的投运。
据悉，虽然海伦公司尚未最终敲定核供热厂的建造决定，仍需完成环境影响评估(EIA)、详细选址调查及技术路线最终选择，但该项目已受到欧洲海事与能源领域的广泛关注。与德国在2023年全面关停核电且缺乏SMR政策框架不同，赫尔辛基如果成功落地该项目，将为欧洲乃至全球城市区域供热提供一种全新的无碳基荷热源示范路径。

波兰政府通过“新版核电计划”，建设6-9吉瓦核电机组
2026年10月5日，波兰政府正式通过新版核电计划，确认建设两座大型核电站，目标装机约6至9吉瓦。首座Lubiatowo-Kopalino核电站位于波罗的海沿岸北部波美拉尼亚省(Pomerania)，采用三台西屋电气(Westinghouse)AP1000机组，首罐核混凝土计划2028年浇筑，三台机组商运时间分别为2036年、2037年和2038年，较2020年版推迟，但机组间隔由两年缩短为一年。
据了解，该项目已从准备阶段转入实施阶段，国有项目公司波兰核电站公司(Polskie Elektrownie Jądrowe, PEJ)于2026年3月向核监管机构PAA(Państwowa Agencja Atomistyki, PAA)提交建设许可申请。波兰为2025至2030年安排602亿兹罗提(约136亿欧元)国家股权，股权覆盖项目成本30%，其余70%来自国家担保的债务融资，欧盟委员会(European Commission)已于2025年12月批准该支持模式。
第二座核电站EJ2计划2027年选定战略伙伴和反应堆技术，2028年确定厂址，2032年浇筑首罐核混凝土，首批两台机组目标2040年和2041年商运。EJ2将采用大型第三代+(Generation III+)水冷反应堆技术，法国、加拿大和美国参与对话，首选厂址为中波兰的贝乌哈图夫(Bełchatów)和科宁(Konin)煤电基地，东部的科杰尼采(Kozienice)和东南部的波瓦涅茨(Polaniec)也列入分析。新版计划设定首台机组按价值计算至少40%国内产业参与率，后续机组预计提高;国家计划之外的小型模块化反应堆(Small Modular Reactors, SMR)项目应作为补充，波兰将编制单独的“波兰SMR路线图”。
据悉，该计划正式采纳标志着波兰在退出煤电、提升能源安全方面迈出关键一步，并将影响其核电供应链与区域煤电转型节奏。

BWXT先进微堆BANR获选加拿大可运输核电站项目：打造G7首座商用可移动核电工程
BWX技术公司(BWX Technologies, Inc., 简称BWXT)于2026年10月5日宣布，加拿大清洁能源开发商Prodigy Clean Energy、帕比诺原住民族(Pabineau First Nation)及鳗河坝原住民族(Eel River Bar First Nation)已正式选定BWXT的BANR微反应堆(Microreactor)技术，用于在加拿大新不伦瑞克省贝尔杜恩(Belledune, New Brunswick)建设一座可运输核电站(Transportable Nuclear Power Plant, TNPP)。
该试点工程由原住民族主导并全资持有，选址位于帕比诺和鳗河坝原住民族的传统领地内，规划建设装机容量最高达50兆瓦电功率(MWe)的全尺寸Prodigy可运输核电平台。项目旨在全面验证移动式核电站的厂址物流与标准化运维规范，为未来在加拿大北部偏远地区及全球出口市场批量部署TNPP舰队确立商业与工程蓝图。新不伦瑞克省政府已向Prodigy及原住民族联合体正式出具具有法律效力的承购意向书(Letter of Intent, LOI)，承诺全额消纳该电站所发电力，项目瞄准2030年代初实现商业投运。
入选的BWXT先进核反应堆(BWXT Advanced Nuclear Reactor, BANR)属于紧凑型高温气冷堆(High-Temperature Gas-Cooled Reactor, HTGR)，单堆设计热功率为75兆瓦(MWt)，电功率约为22兆瓦(MWe)。堆芯采用高丰度低浓缩铀(High-Assay Low-Enriched Uranium, HALEU)包裹的三层各向同性包覆颗粒燃料(Tri-structural Isotropic Particle Fuel, TRISO)，具备全非能动冷却与模块化灵活能量转换特性，能够在全厂断电等极端工况下依靠自然物理机制保障固有安全。
Prodigy的TNPP体系架构专注于实现反应堆在数十年全生命周期内的集装化安全部署。该移动基础设施可根据用能负荷集成单个或多个BANR机组，核心模块实现100%工厂化预制并通过海运或陆路整体运输至现场。整装抵港后现场组装与安装工期预计仅需18个月左右，随后即可直接进入装料与带核调试阶段。
依托加拿大CANDU重水堆大修及新建机组积累的产业工人与成熟供应链，BWXT加拿大公司(BWXT Canada Ltd.)及其控股的工程服务公司Kinectrics将全面主导该工程的制造与交付。贝尔杜恩项目的两台BANR机组及常规岛辅助系统(Balance of Plant, BOP)将主要在BWXT位于安大略省的工厂内加工制造。安大略省能源与矿业部长斯蒂芬·莱切(Stephen Lecce)对此高度评价，指出该项目代表着七国集团(G7)首个面向商业化运行的可移动微堆工程，展现了加拿大在下一代前沿核能产业上的引领地位。
目前，BWXT与Prodigy正加速推进项目工程设计、核安全许可审查、供应链深度融合及投融资结构的最终协议签署。双方计划以贝尔杜恩试点为范本，面向全球商业电网、离网高能耗工业基地及国防能源保障等多元场景，规模化推广BANR可运输核电系统。

菲律宾总统马科斯将访问新加坡 推介投资优先项并考察核能与安全合作
近日，菲律宾总统费迪南德·马科斯(Ferdinand Marcos Jr.)应新加坡总理黄循财(Lawrence Wong)邀请，将于10月7日至11日对新加坡进行工作访问。期间，马科斯总统将出席福布斯全球CEO大会(Forbes Global CEO Conference)，向来自新加坡及全球的470多位商界领袖推介菲律宾的投资机会，并实地考察新加坡在核能与安全领域的专业经验。
据报道，菲律宾外交部(Department of Foreign Affairs, DFA)助理部长阿纳林·拉托内尔(Aanalyn Ratonel)在发布会上表示，总统此次参会将重点聚焦能够推动菲律宾国家经济增长的关键行业，包括数字技术、人工智能、先进制造业、基础设施、能源以及医疗保健等领域。拉托内尔表示，随着菲律宾人工智能及数据中心(Data Center)等高耗能产业对电力需求的急剧增长，探索清洁可靠的核能发展路径显得尤为关键。
据了解，访问期间小马科斯总统还将专程参访新加坡核研究与安全研究所(Singapore Nuclear Research and Safety Initiative, SNRSI)，深入了解新加坡在核能研究、核安全(Nuclear Safety)及监管框架方面的成熟做法。菲方表示，此类双边交流有助于支持菲律宾的长期能源规划，并在核科学、安全监管及人才能力建设方面创造深层次的合作机遇。
据悉，本次访问也正值东盟(ASEAN)轮值主席国交接的前夕。两国将在经济一体化、数字经济、能源与粮食安全等优先领域开展密切协作。新加坡作为菲律宾的核心经济伙伴，2025年双边贸易额已达92.7亿美元(USD)，且在2026年上半年成为菲律宾投资委员会(Board of Investments, BOI)批准的最大外国投资承诺来源国，

田纳西河谷管理局Sequoyah核电站开始燃料更换及维护
2026-10-06 17:21 TVA Sequoyah核电站
2026年10月5日，田纳西河谷管理局(Tennessee Valley Authority, TVA)对位于索迪-戴西(Soddy-Daisy)的Sequoyah核电站进行燃料更换和年度维护。
据介绍，燃料更换是核电站正常运行的一部分，涉及将乏燃料取出并更换为新的燃料组件。维护工作包括对各种设备和系统进行检查、测试和维修，以确保核电站的安全可靠运行。
受此次停堆检修影响，Sequoyah核电站在此期间将暂停发电。为应对由此产生的电力缺口，田纳西河谷管理局将通过其现有的多元化发电组合调度其他资源予以补足，并与区域电网运营商保持紧密对接，全力将对电网供应的影响降到最低。
除了常规的燃料更换与设备检修，田纳西河谷管理局还在Sequoyah核电站同步推进多项技术改造和升级项目，着力提升电站的安全防护水平与整体运行效率。具体改进措施涵盖安全系统的升级换代、全新监控设备的安装投用，以及日常维护程序和执行规范的优化。

美国能源部承诺42亿美元贷款，支持Vistra核电站扩容升级
2026年10月5日，美国能源部(Department of Energy, DOE)能源主导融资办公室(Office of Energy Dominance Financing)宣布，承诺提供最高42亿美元有条件贷款，资助维斯特拉公司(Vistra Corp.)在宾夕法尼亚州(Pennsylvania)和俄亥俄州(Ohio)的核电站扩容与现代化改造。
据了解，此项投资旨在执行美国总统唐纳德·特朗普关于“重振核工业基础”的行政命令。美国能源部长克里斯·赖特(Chris Wright)表示，通过提高现有核电站发电量，可为美国家庭和企业提供负担得起、可靠且全天候可用的电力。
项目还包括法国电力公司(Électricité de France, EDF)的有条件承诺，即提供贷款选项，为维斯特拉位于得克萨斯州(Texas)的科曼奇峰核电站(Comanche Peak Nuclear Power Plant)可能增加的容量提供融资。该计划将维持约4吉瓦可靠基荷核电容量，足以供应超过300万户家庭，并新增433兆瓦核电容量。相关投资预计支持约3000个工程、建筑和计划停堆维修岗位，同时保留数千个永久性高薪岗位。维斯特拉计划升级宾夕法尼亚州比弗谷核电站(Beaver Valley Nuclear Power Station)、俄亥俄州戴维斯-贝西核电站(Davis-Besse Nuclear Power Station)和佩里核电站(Perry Nuclear Power Plant)，并支持这些机组在现有许可证到期后再运行20年。
据悉，该贷款若最终落地，将在人工智能与数据中心用电快速增长的背景下强化PJM电网基荷电源保障，并为美国现有核电站延寿增容提供新的融资范式。

欧洲完成ITER真空容器最后扇形体交付，16年制造收官
近日，聚变能源组织(Fusion for Energy, F4E)与安萨尔多核能公司(Ansaldo Nucleare)、西屋电气公司(Westinghouse)和沃尔特·托斯托(Walter Tosto)合作，已完成国际热核聚变实验堆(ITER)欧洲最后一个真空容器(Vacuum Vessel)扇形体的制造，并将其运抵法国东南部卡达拉什(Cadarache)项目现场。
据了解，ITER真空室内部容积为1400立方米，由九个楔形钢制扇形体组成，每个扇形体高逾14米、重达440吨。组装完成后，真空室外径19.4米、高11.4米、重约5200吨;安装包层和偏滤器等内部组件后，总重量将达8500吨。真空室扇形体由欧洲承担五个、韩国承担四个。2016年双方达成补充协议，韩国增造两个原属欧盟的扇形体，并于2024年11月完成四个扇形体交付。该组件是ITER现场接收的最后一个大型组件，此次交付标志着历时16年的制造工作圆满结束。
F4E总监马克·拉谢斯(Marc Lachaise)表示，在当前聚变竞赛中，知识与专业技能至关重要。得益于F4E、安萨尔多核能公司、西屋电气公司和沃尔特·托斯托组成的联合体紧密合作，并借鉴了ITER韩国项目在部件制造中的经验。最后一个扇形体从西屋电气位于意大利蒙法尔科内(Monfalcone)的工厂出发，由达赫尔公司(DAHER)运至卡达拉什后经海陆联运已安全抵达ITER现场。
ITER旨在建造一座托卡马克(Tokamak)聚变装置，验证聚变作为大规模无碳能源的可行性。其目标是在50兆瓦等离子体加热功率输入下，以500兆瓦功率运行至少400秒，运行中可能还需额外300兆瓦电力输入，ITER本身不产生电力。35个国家参与合作，欧盟承担近一半建设成本，中国、印度、日本、韩国、俄罗斯和美国平均分担剩余部分。ITER于2010年开工，首次等离子体运行时间已从原计划2018年推迟，修订后的计划提出2035年实现氘-氘聚变运行。

title: 科学网-谈新科物理学诺奖得主：他支持中国深海中微子望远镜
content:
谈新科物理学诺奖得主：他支持中国深海中微子望远镜
北京时间10月6日17时45分，2026年诺贝尔物理学奖揭晓，弗朗西斯·哈尔岑（Francis Halzen）获奖，表彰他对冰立方中微子天文台的决定性贡献，以及发现源自天体的高能中微子。
哈尔岑1944年出生于比利时，1969年获得比利时鲁汶大学博士学位。诺贝尔委员会评价，他为一种全新的天文学奠定了基础，他设想利用南极的冰川冰来捕获被称为中微子的神秘粒子。其成果便是冰立方中微子观测站（IceCube Neutrino Observatory）——它能够追踪来自遥远宇宙的中微子。
“他有非常强的人格魅力，也非常纯粹。在纷繁的大型科学合作组里，他永远把科学放在第一位。他就是这样坚定——科学放在第一位，把我们紧紧团结在一起。他永远为那些疯狂的想法而激动，也永远支持年轻人。”自2009年就在IceCube开展研究的徐东莲告诉澎湃科技，在IceCube学习工作的十几年里，哈尔岑对她的影响是巨大的。
如今，徐东莲是上海交通大学物理与天文学院副教授、李政道研究所长聘学者、南海中微子望远镜项目（海铃计划）发起人和首席科学家，“我们在南海建的海铃望远镜，目标是比IceCube提升10倍的能力、分辨三种不同中微子。建成后会有全新的突破，产生重大科学成果。”
一立方公里南极冰捕捉“幽灵粒子”
中微子是构成物质世界最基本的粒子之一。被称为“幽灵粒子”的它，携带着宇宙最深处的奥秘。中微子的诞生往往与宇宙中的极端事件有关，例如宇宙大爆炸、超新星爆发、双中子星并合、黑洞爆发等。其中，高能中微子主要源于宇宙射线与尘埃和气体的碰撞。
普通的宇宙粒子在穿梭宇宙的过程中，会被星际气体、尘埃遮挡，还会被宇宙磁场偏转路线，抵达地球时早已丢失大量原始信息。而中微子则截然不同，它几乎不与任何物质发生反应，穿越茫茫宇宙、恒星星体甚至地球本体都畅通无阻，飞行过程中不会跑偏方向、也不会损耗能量。
徐东莲告诉澎湃科技，中微子是一种不带电的基本粒子，穿透力极强。即便在极端宇宙中那些致密到连光都无法穿透的区域，它也能轻易逃逸而出。因此，中微子是探索极端宇宙非常理想的信使。
但中微子携带的宇宙信息，是人类依靠望远镜、电磁波等所有传统观测手段都无法获取的。
“捕捉它也非常难了，因为它都不怎么爱反应，就跟过无人之境一样。”徐东莲说，以IceCube南极实验为例，假设有100万个高能中微子穿过，平均大约只有一个会发生反应。“它跟光不一样，光穿过去你都能看见，中微子穿过去都不反应，所以很难捕捉。即使它发生反应，也是与原子核中的夸克相互作用，释放出微弱的蓝光。”
正因如此，探测中微子需要极为纯净透明、体量庞大的天然介质，例如南极冰川或深海海水。
1988年，哈尔岑首次提出在南极捕获中微子的构想。南极的冰不受各类干扰，这里地质稳定，没有地震。哈尔岑和他的构想很快获得了其他研究人员的支持，而仅仅几年后，便在冰中对传感器进行了初步测试。
能量极高的宇宙中微子极为罕见，因此需要极其巨大的冰体量，才能观测到足够数量的碰撞。2011年建成的“冰立方”覆盖了整整一立方公里。研究人员很快发现了首批高能中微子，并在几年后得以发表他们的发现：这些中微子必定源自我们太阳系之外的遥远之处。
徐东莲说，2012年，哈尔岑团队发现了这些来自天外的中微子，证明了中微子确实存在，从而开创了高能中微子天文学这一全新学科领域，也为人类观测宇宙提供了一种全新手段。在极端天体过程中，中微子和引力波往往率先逃逸，它们穿透力极强，能够传播极远的距离，因此，中微子与引力波共同构成多信使天文学时代两大主要驱动的信使。
永远把科学放在第一位，也永远支持年轻人
自2009年以来，徐东莲在南极冰立方中微子观测站（IceCube）开展研究，参与了宇宙高能中微子及首个对应源的发现并作出重要贡献。
“我在IceCube学习工作十几年，哈尔岑对我的影响是巨大的。”在徐东莲眼中，哈尔岑是一位极度纯粹的物理学家。理论物理学家出身的他能够带动一群做实验的人，把一个天马行空的想法一步步落实。他甚至能从柏林街头招募一位弹吉他的编程高手进入团队，搭建起整个分析软件框架。他既有能力对接政府高层，也擅长与各式各样的人才互动，将他们招至麾下，为那个天马行空的想法共同创造。而所有参与其中的人，都乐在其中。
“他有非常强的人格魅力，也非常纯粹。在纷繁的大型科学合作组里，他永远把科学放在第一位。他就是这样坚定——科学放在第一位，把我们紧紧团结在一起。他永远为那些疯狂的想法而激动，也永远支持年轻人。”
徐东莲说，哈尔岑支持年轻人的“野心”和勇敢的想法，擅长营造一种让所有人都感到愉快、只专注于科学讨论的氛围。无论什么样的思想、什么样的想法，他总是鼓励；无论你的想法多么疯狂，他都鼓励你去试一试。
徐东莲曾指导过哈尔岑的一名研究生。“我们经常去他办公室，带着各种有的没的想法去和他碰撞。有一次，我和他的研究生拿着一个连我们自己都觉得可能不太可行的想法去找他聊，倒不是一定要请他定夺——在科学领域，大家都是在探索，未必需要谁来定夺——而是希望他能和我们一起完成思维的闭环。”
“我们跟他聊了半天，他都是很鼓励，然后我们就回去探索了半年，我发现这事还是太难了。我又回去跟他说这事太难了，我们要再换一个方向，换一个方法。他说，其实当时他就觉得不太行，但是他不想打击我们。”
徐东莲说，哈尔岑就是这样的风格，“他把我们当成一群富有想象力、充满好奇、很有能力、甚至有点天才的小朋友，带着我们一起玩。”
挺进南海，建设中国首个深海中微子望远镜
“IceCube的发现在诺奖的预测风向标里有好几年了。”徐东莲说，今年哈尔岑获得诺贝尔奖，这只是一个开端，与引力波天文学一样仅仅是开始，未来这一领域还会诞生更多诺奖级的成果。
为了捕捉这些“幽灵粒子”，科学家远赴南极冰川，也挺进南海深海。
海铃望远镜构想图。望远镜阵列约有1200条垂直线缆，每条线缆上约有20个光学模块。
2018年，徐东莲回国组建团队，启动了“海铃计划”，探索建设中国首个深海中微子望远镜，通过捕捉高能（亚TeV到PeV量级）天体中微子来探索极端宇宙。诺奖委员会放的视频里，全球中微子望远镜布局中，“海铃计划”赫然在列。
徐东莲说，想要捕获这些近乎“隐身”的中微子，需要一个极其庞大、纯净且处于黑暗环境中的探测器。南海3000米以下的水体，以良好的水质、近乎完全黑暗的环境和天然的屏蔽，成为建设巨型中微子望远镜的理想场所。
2021年9月初，“海铃探路者”项目团队完成首次海试任务，验证了预选海域作为中微子望远镜台址的可行性，为“海铃计划”的后续推进奠定了基础。海铃团队在这些重要结果基础之上，完成了海铃中微子望远镜的概念设计。
2022年底，海铃望远镜项目启动。它选址在我国海域靠近赤道一个深约3.5公里的深海平原，直径约4公里、占地约12平方公里，由1200根线缆组成，预计在2030年前后建成，设计寿命20年。
“我们在南海建的海铃望远镜，目标是比IceCube提升10倍的能力、分辨三种不同中微子。建成后会有全新的突破，产生重大科学成果。”徐东莲表示。
中国科学院院士、海铃望远镜项目负责人景益鹏曾表示，我国在多波段望远镜、空间引力波和低能中微子观测站方面均有布局，海铃高能中微子望远镜将填补我国多信使天文观测网中尚且空缺的重要一环，促进和完善我国多信使天文观测网建设。
海铃望远镜选址在低纬度近赤道地区，随着地球的自转，可360度巡天，与全球范围的其他中微子望远镜形成互补。
“哈尔岑经常会到李政道研究所，也在论坛上公开表达对‘海铃计划’的支持。他曾表示，海铃望远镜计划将为下一代中微子天文开辟新的篇章。”徐东莲说，她从哈尔岑身上学到的，是一种勇敢而执着的精神：再难的事情，只要想法先到了、思想上先抵达了，行动上便尽一切可能调动能动性，团结一切可以团结的人，把事情一步步往前推。只要保持乐观，再难的事也终能做成。
试想，400年前伽利略发明光学望远镜，人类才真正开始借助工具观测天空；到今天，我们对宇宙的理解已经发生了深刻变化。这是一个全新的领域，更是一扇观测宇宙、理解宇宙的全新窗口。“我很激动，也希望更多年轻人能加入我们，就像上世纪八九十年代IceCube启动时那样，吸引了一批有着天马行空想法的年轻人。”
（原标题：对话徐东莲，谈新科物理学诺奖得主哈尔岑：他永远把科学放在第一位，支持中国深海中微子望远镜 ）

title: 科学网-时隔11年再度斩获诺贝尔物理学奖，中微子研究到底有多特别
content:
时隔11年再度斩获诺贝尔物理学奖，中微子研究到底有多特别
2026年诺贝尔物理学奖今天尘埃落定，82岁的比利时裔美国物理学家弗朗西斯·哈尔岑（Francis Halzen）独享本届奖项，表彰他主导搭建冰立方（IceCube）中微子天文台、发现天体物理源高能中微子的开创性贡献。这份奖项不仅是对一项数十年科研工作的认可，更让沉寂11年的粒子物理领域重回诺奖视野。
以现在人类的技术，想要探索宇宙，是不可能亲自奔赴宇宙深处进行观察的。但是，宇宙深处却向人类所在的地球发送来了许多种宇宙“信使”，使得人类可以在地球上了解远方天体的信息。这些信使包括质子、电子、重原子核这类带电宇宙线；可见光、X射线、无线电波等电磁辐射；还有中微子与引力波。不同信使各有局限：带电宇宙线会被宇宙磁场偏转，丢失原本的方向信息；电磁波与带电宇宙线还会被宇宙尘埃、星际介质遮挡，很多剧烈的宇宙事件就此隐藏在黑暗之中。而中微子和引力波不受磁场偏转，也不容易被星际物质阻挡，能够带来完全不一样的观测视角，帮助我们窥见电磁波看不见的极端宇宙。
中微子被称作宇宙中的“幽灵粒子”，它质量极小、不带电荷，几乎不与任何物质发生相互作用，能够轻松穿越恒星、星系乃至整个地球，踪迹极难捕捉。而它又无处不在，太阳、核电站中、地球内部铀、钍等元素的衰变都能大量地产生中微子，甚至每秒钟会有超过100万亿个中微子穿过你的身体，因此，对中微子的研究很重要，能让我们理解我们所在的宇宙一些更底层的自然规律。
宇宙中最剧烈的天体活动，比如黑洞吞噬物质、星系爆发、超新星爆炸等，会带来一些能量远超太阳和地球中微子的超高能中微子，它们不受遮挡、不被偏转，能直线传递宇宙最原始的高能信息，是解锁极端宇宙奥秘的全新密钥。
想要捕捉这些“幽灵粒子”，难度堪称天文级。普通探测器无法捕捉中微子的微弱反应，想要捕捉到中微子撞击某些原子核产生的信号，需要尽可能多的原子核“靶”，因此，中微子探测实验通常都需要建造的非常巨大，装有5万吨超纯水的日本超级神冈实验和装有2万吨液体闪烁体以及4万吨超纯水的中国江门中微子实验都是现代中微子实验的代表。
但是，想要探测那些来自宇宙的超高能量的中微子事件，直径几十米的中微子探测器就显得有些不够用了，因为来自宇宙的超高能中微子产生的带电粒子，能轻易穿过上千米的空间。而哈尔岑凭借超前的科学远见，提出了一个大胆的构想：把南极的天然冰层当作巨大的“靶”，并利用纯净至极的南极冰层搭建巨型探测器。南极冰层深处杂质极少、环境稳定、无人工干扰，是地球上观测中微子的绝佳天然介质。而巨大的南极冰层，可以让有效的探测体积达到立方千米的级别，这成为了探测超高能中微子信号的绝佳场所。
历经数十年攻坚，哈尔岑带领团队在南极冰层下构建起体积达一立方千米的探测网络，植入5160个高精度光学传感器，建成了全球独一无二的“冰立方”中微子天文台。
这套特殊的探测系统工作原理十分精妙：当来自遥远宇宙的超高能中微子穿透地球、撞击南极冰层中的原子核时，会产生一些高速运动的带电粒子，比如电子和缪子。这些带电粒子在冰层中以超过冰层中的光速运动时，会产生微弱的切伦科夫闪光。深埋冰层的传感器会精准捕捉这些转瞬即逝的微光，科学家通过分析闪光的位置、强度和时间，就能反推中微子的能量、来源方向，最终锁定其对应的宇宙天体源。依靠冰立方的持续观测，哈尔岑团队首次确凿探测到来自天体物理源的高能中微子，终结了百年以来宇宙射线起源的谜题，正式开辟出高能中微子天文学这一全新学科领域，让人类的宇宙观测迈入“多信使天文学”新时代。在冰立方实验开始之后，位于俄罗斯贝加尔湖的Baikal-GVD实验、位于地中海的KM3NeT实验、位于中国南海的“海铃”实验等类似的高能中微子望远镜实验陆续开始建设，成为了观测宇宙的重要手段。”
本届诺奖是粒子物理学时隔11年再度斩获诺贝尔物理学奖。上一次粒子物理相关领域获奖是2015年的中微子振荡研究，十余年间，诺奖物理学奖多聚焦于量子信息、凝聚态物理、宇宙学等领域，此次哈尔岑的获奖，让沉寂已久的高能粒子物理重回大众与学界视野。
这也是诺贝尔物理学奖第五次颁发给中微子实验相关的研究，前四次分别是：1、1988年，莱德曼、施瓦茨、斯坦伯格：发现μ（缪）子中微子，证明中微子不止一种，建立中微子束实验方法，确认存在不同“味道”的中微子。2、1995年，莱因斯：直接探测到中微子（电子反中微子）。3、2002年，雷戴维斯、小柴昌俊：探测太阳中微子，并且小柴昌俊的神冈探测器捕捉到1987A超新星爆发的中微子，开创宇宙中微子观测。4、2015年，梶田隆章、麦克唐纳：发现中微子振荡现象，证明中微子具有质量。这是第一个超出粒子物理标准模型的实验证据。
中微子领域一次次摘得诺奖，也足以说明这个“幽灵粒子”的分量：从发现中微子本身，到中微子振荡，再到如今探测来自遥远天体的高能中微子，人类对中微子的每一步重大突破，都在重塑我们对微观粒子和整个宇宙的认知。
其次，这是近半个世纪极为罕见的单人独享物理学诺奖。现代物理学重大突破很多都依托合作项目，科研成果多为团队协作产物，诺奖也形成了多人共享的惯例，21世纪以来物理学奖还没有单人获奖的情况。上一次物理学家独自斩获该奖项还要追溯到1992年，时隔34年。
粒子物理实验，向来是诺贝尔物理学奖的“困难户”。现代粒子物理实验动辄需要成百上千名科研人员协同工作，探测器建造、数据采集、分析都离不开庞大合作组。但诺奖有一条硬性限制：每个奖项最多只能由三人分享。这条规则，在很大程度上阻碍了很多大型粒子物理实验拿到诺奖——哪怕成果本身达到诺奖级别，贡献分散在数百上千人当中，也很难从中选出符合要求的获奖者。
但这条路并非完全封死。如果一项大型实验，存在一位无可替代的灵魂人物，从最初构想、方案论证，到推动项目落地、持续引领整个实验，奖项就有机会授予他。哈尔岑就是典型代表：冰立方是大型国际合作项目，但诺委会认定，整个实验的原始设想与推进，都源于他，因此将奖项单独授予他。
同类型经典案例，就是日本神冈/超级神冈中微子实验。当年诺奖同样是授予实验的核心灵魂人物，而非整个合作组。
从长远价值来看，冰立方中微子天文台的建成和高能中微子的发现，彻底打破了人类传统的宇宙观测边界。此前我们“看宇宙”靠光，如今我们可以依靠中微子穿透黑暗、直击宇宙最极端的高能事件。这项成果不仅帮助人类揭秘宇宙射线的起源、探索极端天体物理过程，更为未来探测未知宇宙现象、破解宇宙演化终极谜题提供了全新路径，为人类探索宇宙打开了一扇全新的窗口。
（作者陈缮真，系中国科学院高能物理研究所青年研究员，博士生导师，欧洲核子研究中心大型强子对撞机LHCb实验成员）

title: 科学网-研究发现“摊大饼”让城市热岛效应更明显
content:
研究发现“摊大饼”让城市热岛效应更明显
随着规模扩张和人口密度增加，城市热岛效应日益成为一项严峻的环境挑战。
近日，复旦大学环境科学与工程系研究员余兆武团队一项覆盖全球一千多座城市的研究显示：城市越来越大未必越来越热，关键在于它怎么“长”。横着长，把“饼”摊大，地面会明显变热；竖着长，把楼房盖高，可明显减轻热岛效应。
“过去判断城市热岛效应只看建筑总量，通常认为建筑面积越大热岛效应越明显。”余兆武告诉《中国科学报》，“我们的研究发现，城市扩展中‘摊大饼’和‘盖高楼’两种建筑方式对地表升温影响巨大。我们完全可以用更合理的建筑类型减轻热岛效应的影响。”
城市扩展中，“摊大饼”是把房子铺开，占用越来越多的土地；盖高楼，在原有地盘上把楼一层层加高。过去的研究把这两件事混在一起看，所以说不清楚城市变热，是“摊得大”还是“盖得高”影响更大。
为了弄清两种建筑模式对地表温度的影响，研究团队收集了2020年全球1480个城市的数据，他们结合建筑档案，把城市划分为1公里大小的方块，利用卫星遥感地面温度数据，分别计算出每小块的地面温度和当地的建房情况，然后把“建筑总量”拆成两个部分：一部分看土地被房子占了多少，另一部分看房子平均盖了多高。最后，分析同样增加一成的建筑量，分别看看地面温度会有什么变化，谁的“热度贡献”更大。
结果很明显，建筑多的地方，地面确实更热，将近四分之三的城市都呈现筑总量越大最热月份地面温度越高的规律。但真正有意思的是拆开之后的对比：增加同样多的建筑量，靠占地“摊大”出来的那部分，对应地面升温约是靠“盖高”那部分的数倍。
发现，建筑占地多的地方，树木、草地和水面就越少，硬邦邦的地面越多。而房子盖得高，常常伴随着更多的绿化和水面。当研究人员把绿化、植被这些因素加进去计算时，占地和升温的关联一下子减弱了很多。
“这说明，‘摊大饼’之所以让城市热，很大程度上就是因为它吞掉了绿色，阳光直接晒在光秃秃的水泥地上导致很快升温；高楼则把土地省下来留给树木和流水，高楼投下的阴影和形成的通风都能给城市降温。”余兆武说，“在超过六成的城市里，都出现了这种情况。也就是说，往增加同量的房子，‘平摊’开比‘叠加’热得多得多。”
为进一步了解环境、建筑和升温的关联，研究人员把卫星数据显示“平摊”升温更快、“盖高”升温更快和两种升温都很明显的城市进行归纳整理。发现在潮湿多雨的热带城市，“摊大饼”和“盖高楼”对升温影响的差别最大；而在干旱少雨的地方，两者的差别会缩小，有时甚至会出现轻微的反转。
“因此，不能说只要盖高楼就一定凉快，也不能说占地就一定热。具体情况还得看当地的植被、气候和地理条件。”余兆武说，“这项研究给城市建设提了个醒，城市要发展，房子要增加，但怎么增加是可以选择的。与其把房子越盖越宽，占据宝贵的绿地和水面，不如把楼往高了盖，把土地留给树荫和流水。高楼投下的阴影、留出的空间，会实实在在地帮城市降降温。”
尽管该研究使用的是一年的卫星温度数据，且地面温度也不完全等于人体感受到的凉热，但全球范围内的大方向已经很清楚。研究人员同时表示，该研究为全球范围的城市内部空间关联，不能据此推断单独提高建筑高度必然降温，或扩大建筑占地必然升温。后续仍需结合多年份建筑形态、更精细的热环境观测和过程模型，检验水平扩张与垂直生长对城市热环境的长期影响。

title: 科学网-刘慈欣科幻童话《烧火工》沉浸体验空间全球首发
content:
刘慈欣科幻童话《烧火工》沉浸体验空间全球首发
9月29日，《烧火工》沉浸体验空间在上海科技馆举行全球发布会。由刘慈欣科幻童话《烧火工》改编的这一综合性沉浸体验项目，将于10月1日起正式开放，大空间VR体验将在
《烧火工》沉浸体验空间将持续开放至2027年8月底。
《烧火工》是刘慈欣创作的首部独立童话作品，讲述少年萨沙为拯救身患重病的冰儿，前往极东岛协助老烧火工修补星辰，最终继承其点燃太阳的使命，故事蕴含对爱、付出与责任的思考。
《烧火工》沉浸体验空间则是上海科技馆首次以科幻为大主题进行策划。以此为载体，上海科技馆将科幻作为连接科学与文化的一个重要切口，也由此探索科学传播如何从知识呈现进一步延伸至想象激发、文化体验和公众参与，让科学、艺术与想象力在公共文化空间中形成新的连接。
整个沉浸体验空间由超过600平方米的艺术展、超过500平方米的VR大空间体验区以及文创空间共同构成，并融合超高清视听、实时渲染、空间计算、无线通信等技术，最高可支持70位观众同时参与。这一综合体验项目进一步改变了观众与故事之间的关系，观众进入故事内部，在空间、视觉、声音和互动中感知作品所构建的世界。
《烧火工》沉浸体验空间。上海科技馆供图，下同
发布会现场，上海科技馆
姜道荣在致辞中表示，科技不断拓展人们想象未来的边界，文化则为想象提供丰富的内涵和表达，科技与文化的相互激发，也为科技馆拓展科学传播的内容和形式提供了新的空间。
刘慈欣与上海科技馆馆长倪闽景围绕“鲸骨火箭——如何将想象力点火升空”展开主题对谈，从《烧火工》创作谈到VR等新媒介的多元表达，并结合科技馆科学教育实践，探讨如何发挥场馆在激发好奇心、想象力和主动探索中的作用，让文学作品中的科幻想象借助新媒介走进公共文化空间，转化为可感知、可参与的体验。
刘慈欣（中）与倪闽景（右
《烧火工》新版绘本特别签字版赠书仪式、《烧火工》VR正式预告片发布仪式等也于活动现场举行。《烧火工》VR作品出品人、导演姬少亭介绍，主创团队与上海科技馆将围绕科幻创作、科学想象与未来探索，持续推出相关主题活动，让一部作品所打开的想象空间进一步延展到更多内容和更多公众之中。
《烧火工》VR正式预告片发布。
上海科技馆“年度科幻榜评选”计划也在现场正式发布。这份榜单将从科幻、科普、科技、艺术等跨界视角进行评选，梳理分析过去十年中国科幻的发展历程，优选出最值得阅读、观看的作品。

title: 科学网-通用AI驱动设计框架为多亚基蛋白界面设计提供新思路
content:
通用AI驱动设计框架为多亚基蛋白界面设计提供新思路
华东理工大学教授郁惠蕾团队提出深度学习驱动的界面设计方法DeepIE，通过识别并重塑多聚体酶的亚基界面提高其稳定性，为多亚基蛋白的界面设计提供了新思路，对设计高效且稳定的多聚体生物催化剂具有借鉴意义。相关研究成果近日发表于《美国化学会-催化》。
界面是由多个相互作用区域共同组成的“分布式网络”，其稳定性来源于多个接触区域之间分散且相互关联的作用，局部构象的波动可能牵一发而动全身，进而波及更广泛的界面相互作用。多聚体结构广泛存在于天然酶中，其中亚基间的界面不仅是各亚基组装的基础，也深刻影响酶的结构稳定性与催化功能。如何在提升稳定性的同时保留酶的催化活性，成为多聚体酶工程长期面临的关键难题。
研究团队建立了由“柔性界面识别—局部序列设计—活性预测筛选”组成的DeepIE方法，实现了对复杂亚基界面的全局重塑。研究团队首先利用分子动力学模拟定位亚基界面中波动最大的区域，将其锁定为改造靶点；随后借助深度学习工具ProteinMPNN对上述区域进行序列重设计；最后引入蛋白质语言模型辅助的活性预测，对海量候选序列进行高效过滤，确保最终进入湿实验的突变体兼具稳定性与催化活性。以二聚体甲酸脱氢酶为例，该方法使酶在50℃下的半衰期延长约500倍，同时保持了催化活性，分子动力学分析则进一步揭示了稳定性提升的分子机制。

title: 科学网-第二届中国非遗数智创新创意大赛在深圳举行
content:
第二届中国非遗数智创新创意大赛在深圳举行
9月16日至17日，以“非遗共融·文明同辉”为主题的“第二届中国非物质文化遗产数智创新创意大赛”在深圳举行。
本届大赛立足中华优秀传统文化与非物质文化遗产资源，全面探索非遗在当代社会的创造性转化和创新性发展。参赛作品内容涵盖非遗数字化展示、智能交互设计、虚拟现实应用、AIGC辅助创作等方向。大赛启动以来，共收到来自全国980个学校的1285个学院共计11806件大学生作品，以及200件社会组投稿，总收稿量为12006件。经严格遴选，20件作品晋级决赛，最终《寻迹神农溪——沉浸式探秘长江脊梁的活态记忆》《歌起陕北·智联三境》获高校组一等奖，《灵眸》获社会组一等奖。
本届大赛的亮点之一是激发广大高校学子以数智科技为“新画笔”，为非遗活化传承注入新的创意与表达，实现了“高新技术”与“传统文脉”的同频共振。例如大学生组作品《寻迹神农溪——沉浸式探秘长江脊梁的活态记忆》，在VR大空间（LBE）中深度还原了国家级非遗“长江峡江号子”的纤夫文明；《弦新》将视线聚焦于岭南七弦琴，构建“器-声-境”三位一体的数智模型，创新了非遗音乐技艺的教育与体验形态；《基于生成式人工智能的莆仙戏脸谱交互设计》搭建手绘交互程序，使用户能够以零门槛的方式参与生成个性化脸谱图案；《潮起英歌舞非遗潮玩》则借助AIGC辅助设计工具跨界赋能，将潮汕英歌舞角色转化为符合Z世代、α世代审美的Q版手办盲盒IP。
全面打通了非遗向大众消费市场转化的“最后一公里”，成为本届大赛的第二个亮点。大赛首次引入企业参与的“社会组”，构建起“文化挖掘——技术转译——商业落地”的数智创意优化链路。例如，社会组作品《剡川武阳·文房雅集》构建了“实体器物+云端研学”双轨矩阵，将营造技艺化作可感知的产品体验，为建筑类非遗从“静态保护”迈向“数字资产衍生”提供了产业转化范本；《灵眸》则以广东醒狮为基，探索出非遗AIGC创作的“人机协作”范式。
在决赛中，参赛团队不仅展示了非遗的数智创意与设计美学，也关注面向商业逻辑作品实践的验证。评委们则从真实的市场逻辑出发，对作品进行全方位的专业探讨。
决赛现场。上海交通大学供图
本次大赛由未来设计师大赛组委会、上海交通大学文创学院文化创新发展研究院、南方科技大学全球城市文明典范研究院主办。

title: 科学网-第四届非物质文化遗产数字传播与创新发展论坛举行
content:
第四届非物质文化遗产数字传播与创新发展论坛举行
9月18日至19日，以“智焕非遗·文明互鉴”为主题的第四届非物质文化遗产数字传播与创新发展论坛在
浸会大学举行。海内外专家学者、业界代表齐聚一堂，围绕非遗数智传播、跨文化交流与可持续发展等主题开展研讨，探索中华非遗由“走出去”向“走进去”、由文化展示向文明对话深化的新路径。
与会人员合影。上海交通大学供图
浸会大学暂任常务副校长刘际明在致辞中指出，智能技术的发展正在拓展非遗保护的研究边界，也对学科协作提出了新的要求。非遗问题的复杂性决定了单一学科难以形成完整回应，本届论坛的重要价值在于形成计算机科学、传播学、社会学等多学科协同的“超学科”研究视域。
大会发起方、上海交通大学文创学院文化创新发展研究院
薛可指出，本届论坛呈现出三个具有学术辨识度的新特点：从“传播”到“互鉴”的研究范式转换，战略传播视角的引入与学科交叉的深化，数字人文方法论对非遗研究的深层重塑。
浸会大学传理学院
钟布表示，在数字时代，可以通过数据资源、新叙事与新视觉让非遗获得新的表达。未来文化遗产研究需要跨越学科、地域与媒介的界限，以开放协同的姿态推动文化传承与创新。
论坛现场，数字国家艺术剑桥学术研究员、新加坡艺术大学拉萨尔创意产业学院学者娜塔莉娅·格林切娃发表题为“人工智能时代遗产媒体的数字软实力”的学术演讲。她强调，在地缘政治不确定性增强、数智技术快速迭代的当下，数字软实力的培育需要激活受众参与，同时需要通过社区赋权与人工智能伦理共同守护文化遗产的人本价值，确保人类在智能时代仍是文化叙事的主体。
圆桌论坛环节，嘉宾们围绕“从文化遗产到文化连接：战略传播、智能媒体与基于地点的参与”这一主题开展跨界对话。他们一致认为，唯有将文化遗产融入当代生活，让公众成为文化实践的参与者，才能使文化遗产在时代发展中焕发持久生命力。
本届论坛共设置四场英文和八场中文分论坛，来自上海交通大学、
浸会大学、伦敦国王学院等海内外高校的学者共同参会交流。学者们结合自身研究视角，共同探讨非遗如何借助智能媒介焕发表达活力、增进理解。
本届论坛由上海交通大学文创学院文化创新发展研究院、

title: 科学网-助力长江文化保护利用，“智渡2.0——长江记忆地图”发布
content:
助力长江文化保护利用，“智渡2.0——长江记忆地图”发布
9月26日，由上海交通大学城镇空间文化与科学研究中心建设的“智渡2.0——长江记忆
”（以下简称“智渡2.0”）正式发布，包括“共忆长江”“寻迹长江”“云游长江”“智绘长江”四个模块，并面向公众提供记忆资料提交、渡口档案查询、沿江文化浏览与人工智能辅助创作等功能。
面向长江国家文化公园建设，智渡2.0所探索的是一种面向大尺度文化遗产保护的新型工作方式。平台以历史渡口为切入口，将分散于文献、
、影像和田野调查中的文化资源重新组织为可阅读、可查询、可体验、可利用的空间知识体系，拓展了人工智能在文化遗产保护中的应用边界，也为流域尺度上的人文资源识别、价值阐释和公共传播提供了新的技术路径。
“智渡2.0——长江记忆
”。上海交通大学供图
“共忆长江”面向公众开放资料提交入口，收集与长江有关的文字、照片、录音和视频，关注渡工、船员、匠人、迁徙者及沿岸居民的日常经验。
“寻迹长江”以长江干流历史客运渡口为主要对象，通过交互
呈现渡口的兴衰、航线、制度与地方记忆。用户可按上游、中游、下游选择江段，检索具体渡口，也可结合内容标签和时间切片查看相关记录。模块以物像、场景、事件组织资料，将地理位置与历史内容对应起来。用户可在模型中点击建筑要素，读取关联图文，也可沿预设路径漫游或调整观察方向，查看码头、建筑及周边环境的空间关系。查阅一处港口时，用户既能阅读相关资料，也能在三维空间中辨认具体建筑与位置。
“云游长江”以沿江行旅组织文化内容，设置“杜甫：诗行长江”影像入口，并以蜀中、峡江、荆江、洞庭、湘江、姑苏等区域展开文化长卷。用户可从上、中、下游进入不同区域，浏览与当地环境和生活有关的图谱内容，也可以在观看过程中进一步查阅船舶、服饰、建筑等要素，了解不同区域的场景特征。
值得一提的是，“杜甫：诗行长江”以杜甫晚年离蜀、出峡、辗转湖湘的行旅为主线，设置“离蜀启渡”“峡江险渡”“平沙舟市”“洞庭风雪”“吴越少年游”“湘江水乡”六幕，将诗歌文本、地理路线与沿江生活场景相结合，通过数字影像呈现长江流域的地域文化及其相互联系，探索人工智能参与长江文化阐释与传播的方式。
“智绘长江”为保护再生提供多方案智能生成、比较与评价，设置循证问答、图像解读、画面生成与三维创建等功能入口，探索人工智能在文化资料理解和视觉表达中的应用。相关功能为文化展陈、教学讨论和叙事设计提供辅助工具，使用者仍需结合原始资料核对生成内容，区分有据可查的历史信息与创作性表达。
